metadata.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
metadata.abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

metadata.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
metadata.abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $\alpha$, LP-$\alpha$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$\alpha$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $\xi$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $\xi$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $\phi$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $\phi$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $\alpha$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $\xi$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $\phi$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $\xi$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.

metadata.title: Spherically Supported Sets with Variable Radii
metadata.abstract: We study closed sets for which, at every boundary point, there exists a containing supporting ball whose prescribed radius may vary from point to point. This extends the notion of spherical support from constant to variable radii. The variable-radius setting presents a new difficulty: unlike the constant-radius case, the intersection of the supporting balls need not be strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii. We overcome this difficulty by associating with every such set a canonical set and an induced radius function determined by the active supporting balls. For continuous prescribed radii, our main result establishes a geometric dichotomy: the original set either coincides with the canonical set and is strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii, or it is contained in the boundary of the canonical set, which is strongly convex with respect to the induced radii. An example shows that the induced radii cannot, in general, be replaced by the prescribed ones in the second alternative. We also recover the constant-radius theory and characterize variable-radius strong convexity in terms of the spherical support of the boundary.

metadata.title: A counterexample to Gale's conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$
metadata.abstract: It is known that for every partition of the sphere $S^2$ of unit diameter into four parts, the largest diameter of a part is at least $\sqrt{(3+\sqrt{3})/6} = 0.88807\dots$, and this bound is attained. The conjecture of D.~Gale (1953) asserts that no set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a larger ratio. In this paper, we construct a $101$-point set $V\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every partition of $V$ into four parts contains a part of diameter greater than $0.88928 \, \operatorname{diam} V$.

metadata.title: Harmonic-Einstein maps and critical metrics for eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian
metadata.abstract: We prove that Clarke critical metrics for the ratio of the first two eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian on a closed manifold with positive Yamabe constant correspond to harmonic--Einstein maps into a sphere. metadata.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
metadata.abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. metadata.title: Dirichlet eigenvalue asymptotics on conformally compact Einstein manifolds
metadata.abstract: We study the first Dirichlet eigenvalues of large geodesic balls and fixed-width boundary layers on conformally compact Einstein manifolds of dimension $n+1.$ For large balls, we determine the exponential rate of convergence when the spectral bottom is less than $\frac{n^2}{4},$ i.e. the bottom of the continuous spectrum. When it equals the bottom of the continuous spectrum, the second coefficient has two possible values, according to whether the continued resolvent is regular or has a pole there. We also give examples with negative Yamabe conformal infinity realizing both threshold alternatives and construct metrics with a Ricci lower bound that have other second coefficients. Under nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity, we also find the exact second coefficient for the nonlinear $p$-Laplacian on large balls. For layers defined by a geodesic boundary defining function, we compute the first correction and show that its sign characterizes nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity.

metadata.title: Affine $G$-multibiquandle modules for colored links I: representability of coloring functors and color-profile polynomials
metadata.abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $G$ be an abelian group, and fix $u\in R[G]^\times$. For each component-labeled oriented link diagram $(D,\sigma)$, we construct a finitely presented $R[G]$-module $M_u(D,\sigma;R[G])$ with a universal affine coloring $U_{D,\sigma}$. Every affine coloring with values in an $R[G]$-module factors uniquely through $U_{D,\sigma}$ by a module homomorphism. Thus the module represents the affine coloring functor. Each specified colored Reidemeister move induces a unique module isomorphism compatible with coloring transport, and the module isomorphism class is a colored-link invariant. The representing modules and universal colorings commute with arbitrary scalar extension, without a flatness assumption. For classical links, simultaneous rescaling of the component labels removes the common deformation unit. For any multibiquandle, associated-biquandle colorings decompose into fibers indexed by component labelings. For finite targets and palettes, we define a color-profile polynomial recording the joint distribution of fiber sizes and numbers of palette labels used, and prove its invariance under oriented link isotopy. In the affine case, the representing modules determine these fibers, and their specialized dimensions determine the coloring counts over finite fields. The color-profile polynomial is not determined, in general, by the full unweighted distribution of coloring-fiber sizes. It therefore retains information beyond the associated-biquandle coloring count.

metadata.title: Isotropy sets of periodic geodesic flows on three dimensional manifolds
metadata.abstract: A classical theorem of Wadsley states that if all geodesics on a Riemannian manifold M are periodic, then they have a common period, and the geodesic flow induces an S^1-action on the unit tangent bundle. Moreover, a conjecture of Berger asserts that this action is free whenever M is simply connected. In this paper, we investigate the Berger conjecture in dimension three by studying the isotropy set of the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow. Using Morse theory for the energy functional on the free loop space of M, we establish two results in this direction. First, we show that all isotropy groups of the geodesic flow have odd order. Second, we prove that the geodesic flow either acts freely on the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ or has at least two singular orbit types. This paper serves as preparation for the subsequent paper The Berger conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds, in which the conjecture is proved in dimension three.

metadata.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
metadata.abstract: Let $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det \Gamma \ge 1$ for all sublattices $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly log-concave, where $\alpha = 2\pi/e$, and $X + \Lambda$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$. Moreover, we show that the existence of such a density $f$ characterizes the assumption on $\Gamma$ up to a constant. There are a few consequences of the above. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ \mu(\Lambda, K) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} \min_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \|x-\lambda\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}{\pi}} \cdot \mathbb{E}_G\, \|G\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,I)$. This implies an $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. Second, we establish as a consequence an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem with an explicit constant.

metadata.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. metadata.title: Mean curvature nonpositivity and rational connectedness
metadata.abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Gauduchon manifold and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on $X$. We establish equivalent conditions for the existence of a Hermitian metric on $E$ with nonpositive mean curvature. Its complement, if nonzero, is HN-negative with respect to every such metric. In particular, a compact Kähler manifold is not uniruled if and only if , for every Gauduchon metric $\omega$, its tangent bundle admits a Hermitian metric with nonpositive $\omega$-mean curvature. We also obtain an uniruledness criterion that includes the case where the maximal slope of $T_X$ is zero, and a Mumford-type characterization of rational connectedness. Under HN-nonnegativity of $T_X$ for one Gauduchon metric, rational connectedness, the vanishing of all holomorphic covariant tensors, and the condition $\kappa^+(X)=-\infty$ are equivalent.

metadata.title: $L^p$-Liouville properties and realizations of Schrödinger operators on incomplete Riemannian manifolds
metadata.abstract: The aim of the paper is to highlight and standardize in a self-contained framework the connections between some properties associated with the Laplace-Beltrami operator on possibly incomplete Riemannian manifolds. metadata.title: Sharp local scalar-curvature rigidity of spherical caps
metadata.abstract: Let $B(\delta)\subset\mathbb S^n$ be a geodesic ball with the round metric $\bar{g}$ of sectional curvature one, where $n\geq3$ and $0<\delta<\pi/2$. We prove local scalar-curvature rigidity under preservation of the induced boundary metric and a one-sided lower bound for the boundary mean curvature. More precisely, every sufficiently small $C^{2,\alpha}$ perturbation $g$ of $\bar{g}$ satisfying $R(g)\geq n(n-1)$ and $H(g)\geq(n-1)\cot\delta$ is round up to a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. Inspired by the scalar--vector--tensor decomposition used in the study of Yamabe compactness, we establish positivity of the Brendle--Marques quadratic form in the divergence-free gauge for variations preserving the induced boundary metric and satisfying the joint linearized constraints $D R_{\bar{g}}(h)=D H_{\bar{g}}(h)=0$. The hemisphere counterexamples of Brendle--Marques--Neves show that the radius range is sharp.

metadata.abstract: We study scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and rotational symmetry, we prove the sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g \le 2n(n-1)\omega_n \bigl(1-v^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)r^{n-2}, \] when $p$ is the rotational origin. metadata.title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
metadata.abstract: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.

metadata.title: Macroscopic Poincaré Inequalities and Weak-Type Characterizations of $p$-Energy Forms
metadata.abstract: For a class of regular strongly local $p$-energy forms on complete doubling metric measure spaces, $1<p<\infty$, we derive a macroscopic Poincaré inequality from a Poincaré inequality and a capacity upper bound at a doubling scale $\Psi$. The macroscopic inequality compares $L^p$-oscillations at any two scales and yields a uniform two-scale comparison $J_s\lesssim J_r$, $0<r<s$, for the Korevaar-Schoen functionals, strengthening their usual weak monotonicity property. Conversely, under a density assumption on compactly supported functions, the macroscopic inequality yields a regular strongly local Korevaar-Schoen $p$-energy satisfying a $\Psi$-Poincaré inequality. We also show that the macroscopic inequality forces lower $p$-scaling of $\Psi$ on scales not exceeding $\mathrm{diam} X$; together with doubling, this gives two-sided power bounds. Finally, we establish a weak-type characterization of the energy domain of Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung type.

metadata.title: Solutions of $x^α+y^α=1$ in $λ$-Cantor sets
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we study the structure of the solutions of $x^\alpha+y^\alpha=1$ with both coordinates in a $\lambda$-Cantor set. We prove that, for any $\alpha>1$, the intersection with the middle-third Cantor set has positive Hausdorff dimension, strengthening the infinitude question posed by Jiang et al. [J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), e70408]. metadata.title: Fixed geodesics of involutions on $3$-spheres
metadata.abstract: Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2\pi$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.

metadata.title: Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
metadata.abstract: We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.

metadata.title: Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces
metadata.abstract: We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ \Gamma=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.

metadata.abstract: For each positive integer $n$, we give a variational construction of a positive Einstein metric on the connected sum of $n$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$, with coupled toric and dihedral symmetries. metadata.title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
metadata.abstract: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.

analysisBasis.abstract: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.

metadata.title: Generalized Kahler BHE threefolds
metadata.abstract: We study the notion of generalized Kahler Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein (GKBHE) manifolds, namely generalized Kähler manifolds for which both Bismut Ricci forms vanish, and we develop a theory for such structures on compact threefolds. We organize the analysis according to the horizontal rank, an invariant taking values in $\{0,1,2\}$ that measures the relative position of the canonical foliations associated with the two Hermitian structures. We characterize the case of horizontal rank $0$ (which corresponds to Kähler Ricci flat geometry) and describe the case of horizontal rank $1$, revealing its close interplay with the steady $\nu$-soliton equation in Kähler geometry. This description also provides a tool for constructing new compact GKBHE threefolds.
